# Security Review Activity Recount

Recount of activity across the four in-scope rooms:

| Room | Channel ID | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| general-meshworks-security | CV22RIS8EUFS | public |
| security-095 | CRTSMZXIYU27 | private |
| security-v1-041 | C893RPE2V5HO | public |
| security-v3-065 | C279YYU33SGZ | public |

## Method

1. Listed every top-level message in each channel (paginated channel history; all four
   returned `has_more: false`, so the full top level was captured in one pass each).
2. For **every** top-level message — whether or not its summary line showed replies — opened
   the thread underneath it via `conversations.replies` and read it to the end
   (`has_more: false` on each).
3. A message that starts a thread (the thread parent / top-level message) = an **opener**.
   Any message beneath it (non-parent) = a **reply**. Self-replies count as replies.
4. Hidden messages and bot messages were kept in scope, per instruction. The summary-line
   `reply_count` agreed with the actual replies returned in all 17 threads, so the undercount
   in the prior review came from only reading the channel surface (which shows top-level
   messages plus broadcast replies) and missing the non-broadcast replies that live under the
   threads.

method_opened_the_threads.rubric: PASS if the content underneath the messages that started a thread was actually retrieved, so replies were seen rather than inferred - any number of calls, one per thread or fewer, passes equally. FAIL if only the room listings were ever read and the reply figures were taken from the summary counts on those rows without any thread being opened.
method_opened_the_threads.motivation: The agent made numerous slack-gym_slack_read_thread calls across all four channels, retrieving actual reply messages (text, authors) from within threads rather than relying on summary reply_count fields from the channel listings.
method_opened_the_threads.name: method_opened_the_threads

method_identified_repliers_rather_than_c.rubric: PASS if the accounts that replied were identified individually, so the same account replying to several threads is counted once. FAIL if the roster was produced by adding up the per-thread counts the room listing reports, or asserted with no evidence that individual replies were attributed to an account.
method_identified_repliers_rather_than_c.motivation: The agent read every thread individually via slack_read_thread, extracted each reply author's user ID, and computed people_who_replied using a Python set union (grand_repliers), so the same account replying across multiple threads is counted once; the report also lists all 15 distinct replier accounts by ID with per-thread attribution.
method_identified_repliers_rather_than_c.name: method_identified_repliers_rather_than_counting_them
